claims.claim: Reviewers mention that adding mods significantly improves visual quality and overall gameplay.

citations.review_text: This game is so cool from space, with mods it is so much cooler. It is very fun to build things when u figure out how to build nice ships. It can get kinda tricky to know what to do when you are in space, so I would reccomend joining the discord server to learn from other people. 9/10 gets addicting but can also be tricky sometimes

Amazing game, with mods that is. Without mods however, you could almost rate it as somewhat mediocre to just okay.

To make matters worse the studio behind it got fired, and it's been abandoned. Don't expect any updates realistically, and just know you are throwing your money into the void if you buy this, who knows where it goes at this point. And god forbid don't even think about trying the insanely unfinished and even more abandoned "sequel".

It also very much shows it's age without mods, very much based on old space industry pre-SpaceX shaking everything up. Don't expect to be able to make reusable rockets very easily or at all without mods, you can't even switch controls to another stage to land it so good luck with that one. 

Additionally the games physhics engine can sometimes be a pain. Rockets constantly love to wobble unless you spam struts everywhere, or enabled "Advanced Tweakables" in the games settings. This is quite unrealistic, massive rockets in real life such as Starship, New Glenn, and hell even the Saturn V, and N1 for all it's problems never had this issue.

---

However, there is good news on the horizon if you are willing to wait. The developers that got fired along with some former SpaceX people to my understanding, are making a new game called Kitten Space Agency with more of a focus on realism as well. While at it's current state it's more of tech demo, it's being actively worked on and seems very promissing so far. It's already solved many of the issues KSP has, and made some nice improvements on some systems, like SRBs not being set sizes but segments that can be stacked for example much like real life. 

It is made from the ground up on a in-house engine that is actually made for this type of game... Oh did I mention KSP is in Unity, and that causes a ♥♥♥♥ ton of issues and they pretty much had to use hacks to work around the engines limitations? Yeah.

You also have alternatives like Juno New Origins, but I haven't teste…

Amazing, this game is a must have for space enjoyers with lots of times on their hands, you need to actually think about how much your rocket weights, how much fuel you're taking, aerodynamics, even the way you execute manouvers to get from point A to point B. While it isn't in the base game, I HIGHLY recommend using mods to be able to get an even funner experience while playing KSP.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires watching tutorials, reading external material, or facing a steep initial learning curve to understand orbital physics and mechanics.

citations.review_text: Only game I've ever played that got me to buy a textbook (Fundamentals of Astrodynamics by Bate, Mueller, White, and Saylor). One of the best games ever made, with an unfathomably based modding scene a decade later. We may never get anything this good again!

My favorite non-story game! Over 1,500 hours including my xbox, where I spent the bulk of my playtime since 2015. Definitely took time to get even semi-decent at this, but it's amazing and addictive once you get past the hurdles. Due to occasional glitches and lack of some much needed features, I would recommend downloading CKAN and making a good mod list, especially once you've learned the basics of the game. Still, this game will always have it's own corner of my heart. 9.5/10

sit at your desk and watch tutorials and learn orbital physics and get migraines and finally witness the fruits of your labor once you complete a mission successfully.

or alternatively send green guys into the sun at 15,000 m/s

if your into sci fi or if your creative, this game is perfect for you, building spacecraft and downloading different mods i feel like is the best part of this game, i would say its pretty hard at first so i would search up a few tutorials and when you learn that, you basically just go to the next planet

It's hard to get into the game at first, but it's really fun once you get the hang of it. It took quite a while for me to get good at it, but maybe you'll learn quicker than me, haha. Just don't let it overwhelm you, take your time and practice, you'll get the hang of it eventually. But anyway, it's a cool and fun game, and it feels nice landing on the Mun for the first time, planting a flag and looking back at your lander. I could say more, but I'll probably write like several paragraphs. ;-;
One more thing though, don't get ksp2, it's not worth it. Alr, I'm done yapping now. :p

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game has a vibrant modding community that significantly expands gameplay through visual updates, survival mechanics, and parts.

citations.review_text: Great game, with endless amount of mods, including graphical updates whoever wants a fresher feeling.

Only game I've ever played that got me to buy a textbook (Fundamentals of Astrodynamics by Bate, Mueller, White, and Saylor). One of the best games ever made, with an unfathomably based modding scene a decade later. We may never get anything this good again!

A very unique game that teaches you space mechanics, a perfect sandbox, with mods you can go as deep as you want
The modding community for this game is amazing, you can completely transform the game with mods like RSS (real solar system), visual mods like volumetric clouds, there's even a multiplayer and VR mod
Been playing and following it since 2011 but only got it on steam last year, totally worth it
Don't buy KSP-2, we pretend it doesn't exist

Fun game to play and design rockets, planes and whatever your mind desires. Just wish there were more survival mechanics and could do more on the other planets. I do use the Kerbalism mod, which does a good job with survival and part faliures etc.

The game itself is beautiful. But the real reason that this game is still good is the mods. The mods literally range from small asteroids to giant black holes. I 100% reccommend this game. 

The price is really high so aim to get it on sales

After 1 month of playing and 300 hours of playtime, 1 Kerbal killed (it was Jeb RIP), Many rockets, missions, stations and satellites that failed... I finally landed on the mun with Carlie and Bill and they safely returned, finally...

So i definitly recommend buying this game:)

My mods: Kerbalism, Comunity tech tree, Probes before crew, BetterEarlyTree, Outer Planets, Far Future, Near Future, Kerbal Construction Time, Krash, ScanSat, Contract Configurator, MechJeb2, Astrogator, Crew R&R, Deepfreeze, AmpYear, Docking Port Alignment, Restock, Restock+
It's pretty good. Better with mods.

This game is endlessly fun and interesting, from learning to get to orbit to the extensive modding community to doing a crewed return from Eve, there's endless possibilities. This game is vastly improved by the modding community, don't buy KSP 2! KSP 1 with mods is vastly superior in every way.

I have so many hours on this game because its just so wonderful. The base game is kinda bad once you start modding it. Mods are so easy to install after a short youtube video and it changes the game completely. Visual mods make the game look like it was made in 2026, and parts mods gives you the ability to make increadible rockets. It is so fun and I just love how beautiful this game is. I have landed on several planets, and this game has even helped me  conceptualize orbital mechanics which i needed to know for my college physics classes. Wonderful game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that time-warping can trigger glitches known as Kraken attacks.

citations.review_text: I'm one of the new players from the Artemis II launch influx of new players, and I think I'll be here to stay with this amazing timeless game. I would recommend! If you get this game I would recommend making Frequent quick saves because Kraken attacks happen allot when you time warp. It also runs well because It's an old game, however the graphics are still pretty decent. The KSP community and creators are cool too.

Sent Bill on a tiny ship to collect a sample from an asteroid. Didn't realise how fast asteroids moved. Jammed the time warp button accidentally. The tiny ship is now on a top of the line interstellar probe. Bill will not be returning.
